supporting_observations.claim: The reported PowerShell window time, around 13:40 UTC, falls within the stated WS-MLOPEZ-01 winsec and Sysmon collection outage from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; the available records do not show what process, if any, caused the reported window.

At 13:44 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 accessed download.windowsupdate.com through the proxy with a Windows Update Agent user agent and approximately 38.8 MB received, consistent with the organization's stated business-hours patching practice.

At 13:57 UTC, FILE-HD-01 resolved WS-MLOPEZ-01 and then connected to its port 135. This is an unusual remote-management lead given the stated practice that remote administration is only done from WS-OHADDAD-01, but these records do not establish what the connection did.

After endpoint logging resumed, GoogleDriveFS.exe ran as maria.lopez from a Google Drive File Stream installation. Google Drive is not among the organization's approved cloud-storage services; the process record does not show that data was uploaded.

At 14:11–14:12 UTC, svchost.exe accessed LSASS, and a short-lived conhost.exe process ran as SYSTEM with csrss.exe as its parent. These records alone do not establish malicious activity or link either process to the reported PowerShell window.
At 14:04 UTC, proxy records show maria.lopez browsing Stack Overflow and its static-content domain, rather than evidence of a file transfer in those records.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status metadata reports a winsec and Sysmon collection outage on WS-MLOPEZ-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, covering the reported PowerShell appearance; that metadata has no record ID.
Available proxy, Zeek connection, and DNS telemetry does not identify the process responsible for endpoint network activity.
The available records do not provide the command line, parent process, or execution result for any PowerShell activity during the reported time.
claims_not_established: Whether a PowerShell process actually ran around 13:40 UTC, and if so, its command line, parent, user, or purpose.
Whether the FILE-HD-01 connection to port 135 resulted in remote management, code execution, or any other action on WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Whether Google Drive File Stream transferred or synchronized data, or whether its presence had an authorized business explanation.
Whether the LSASS access and conhost.exe activity were related to the reported window or to the FILE-HD-01 connection.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover WS-MLOPEZ-01 endpoint telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including process creation, PowerShell operational/script-block logs, command-line auditing, and EDR events.
Review FILE-HD-01 logs and RPC/WMI or remote-management telemetry around 13:57 UTC to determine the purpose and outcome of the connection to WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Check Google Drive File Stream installation, execution, proxy/network activity, and synchronization or upload logs; confirm whether there was an approved exception.
Obtain the user's account of the window's exact time and appearance and compare it with recovered endpoint evidence.
